key_insight: Trigonal selenium appears intrinsically defect-tolerant: even though point defects create deep gap states, both nonradiative and radiative defect-assisted recombination are too weak to explain the observed efficiency losses.
engineering_relevance: This suggests t-Se is a promising wide-band-gap absorber for tandem and indoor photovoltaics, with defect engineering less critical than in many other emerging materials.
method: First-principles calculations on a large, chemically diverse set of point defects in trigonal selenium
Quantification of defect-assisted Shockley-Read-Hall recombination rates under radiative and nonradiative pathways
Analysis of trends versus defect level position, lattice relaxation, charge state, and doping conditions
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that recombination is strongly suppressed by large lattice reorganizations and energy releases of at least 0.5 Eg per event, and that realistic defect concentrations cannot account for the observed device losses.
watch_item: The conclusion is based on computed defect and recombination models, so real-device performance may still depend on processing, microstructure, and defect populations not fully captured in the calculations.
paper_title: Defect Tolerance in Trigonal Selenium Photovoltaics
